s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly progressive gait disturbance with spinal cord compression
salient_findings: Decreased sensation from the T3 dermatome downward
Clonus and hyperreflexia in the lower extremities
Profound ataxia
Diffusely enhancing lesion centered at T1 with epidural extension
Expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body
key_facts: 1-week history of rapidly progressive gait disturbance
No back pain, fevers, night sweats, or weight loss
No history of smoking or known malignancy
Full strength throughout all extremities
Decreased sensation from the T3 dermatome downward
Four beats of clonus bilaterally
Hyperreflexia in the lower extremities
Profound ataxia
Unable to walk more than a few steps
Contrast-enhanced MRI showed diffusely enhancing lesion at T1
CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis showed no evidence of primary malignancy
Laboratory studies, including inflammatory markers, were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive spinal cord compression with a diffusely enhancing lesion and bony involvement

shortlist.label: Metastatic lung cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Spinal cord compression with an expansile bony lesion, although no primary malignancy was found

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Midline spinal location and expansile bony lesion with epidural extension

shortlist.label: Plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Solitary bony lesion with spinal cord compression and no evidence of systemic disease

shortlist.label: Metastatic breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Spinal cord compression with a diffusely enhancing lesion, although no primary malignancy was found

raw.rationale: The presence of an expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the left pedicle and posterior elements, as seen on CT scans, is more characteristic of a chordoma, which is a rare bone tumor that can cause spinal cord compression and neurological symptoms.

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms such as bone pain, fevers, night sweats, and weight loss, which are absent in this case

rejected.label: Metastatic lung cancer
rejected.why: Patient has no history of smoking or known malignancy, and CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis showed no evidence of primary malignancy

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with a solitary bone lesion, but the absence of systemic symptoms and the specific location and characteristics of the lesion make chordoma more likely

rejected.label: Metastatic breast cancer
rejected.why: There is no mention of a history of breast cancer, and the characteristics of the lesion are not typical of breast cancer metastasis
